PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS / PLACEMENT STUDY

Same wheel.
Six places to hold it.

Where the Quick Action Wheel lives decides how far the thumb travels, which chart it changes and which gesture it collides with. Six placements, compared on a rebuild of the Sahi split chart.

01 / Summary

Summary and the decision needed

PRD v1.4 puts the Quick Action Wheel on the timeframe pill of each chart (V1 below). On the index chart that pill sits in the top 15% of the screen, about 128 mm from the corner a right thumb pivots on. That is out of one-handed reach on a 6.5-inch phone. Its quarter fan also gives each action a 6.6 mm target, smaller than the 7 mm people need even at the centre of the screen. A long-press on the candles is already the crosshair, which you confirmed, so the wheel can't open by holding the chart itself.

This document compares six places to anchor the same seven-action wheel. The comparison uses a working prototype rebuilt from your four Sahi screenshots: the 412×915 Android screen matches within 1–3 px, and the candles were read pixel by pixel from your chart. Every number below comes from the prototype's own geometry on four phone sizes. No user-study results are claimed.

PlacementHold to openShapeActs onReach (max)TargetMain risk

V2 Axis-corner fanCorner where the axes meetQuarter fan, up-leftThat chart100 · 37 mm6.6 mmOption corner sits in Android’s home-swipe strip
V3 Price-axis arc dropAnywhere on the price axisHalf ring, left, at finger heightThat chart47–112 mm7.1 mmInvisible; clashes with axis scaling, the Android back swipe and the hold-to-trade gesture other brokers use

Recommendation

Test V1 (control), V4, V5 and V6 with traders using the prototype's timed tasks, and drop V3. If something has to ship before that study, ship V4 alongside V1. V4 adds no new chrome, makes the chart choice part of the gesture, has the largest targets and fits every phone. V1 stays for single-chart layouts and for people who expect the pill. V5 is the alternative if the dial fails its guardrails: its reach is the best by far, but it puts a permanent button on the chart and picks the chart implicitly. See Section 09 for the decision rule.

New in v1.1 · 9 November 2026

Long names (Section 15). A stress test of every label in all six placements found that the v1.0 labels spill out of their slots even with the defaults (16 of 63 slots). With long preset names they run into each other, and the readout in the centre of the wheel can’t hold a full name. The prototype now fits each label (one or two lines, then a short label, then smaller type) and reads the full action out in a pill outside the wheel. If a label still can’t fit, the hold opens Quick actions instead. Now 0 of 63 slots spill in every set, on both phone sizes. Prior art (Section 16). No trading app we found uses this gesture. MetaTrader 5’s radial chart menu, opened with a tap, is the closest. In Kite, FYERS and Angel One, a hold on a price or on the price axis already means “place an order here”.

Decisions needed from you

1. Approve the study shortlist (V1, V4, V5, V6) and the decision rule. 2. Say whether a permanent floating button on the chart (V5) is acceptable for Sahi. 3. Confirm two facts about the real app: whether the axis corner cell and a hold on the price axis or split handle do anything today (assumed free; OQ-1). 4. Agree the label rules in Section 15, in particular a six-character budget for short labels and opening Quick actions at 200% text.

02 / Problem

What PRD v1.4 left open

  • Reach. v1.4 assumed the pill was the only anchor. The index chart's pill is at 14% of screen height. People who hold the phone in one hand (Hoober: 49% of observed use) have to regrip or use the other hand to reach it, and the fan then opens further up and left.
  • Fit. The 264–280 radius gate passes on every phone with the chart-only layout in your screenshots. It barely passes in an iPhone Safari tab (R 265–266) and fails with the order panel open (v1.4, C-01). A placement that needs less room would remove the fallback cases.
  • Target size. Seven slots in 90° give 11.9° each. At the label radius that is 6.6 mm across, below the 7 mm Hoober measured at the screen centre and well below the 9–12 mm he measured at edges and corners, where the pill and its fan sit.
  • Labels. v1.4 lets people bind any interval and other VWAP and EMA presets, and asked for “EMA / 20” on two lines (C-02). The v1.0 prototype drew every label on one line at a fixed radius. Section 15 tests what happens with longer names and larger text.
  • Gesture budget. The candle area is taken: tap, drag to pan, pinch to zoom, and long-press for the crosshair (confirmed). The price axis scales on drag, the time axis zooms on drag, and the split handle resizes on drag. Any new anchor has to share space with one of these or add a control.
03 / Research

What the research says about placing a radial menu

#FindingWhat it means for Sahi
R1Pie menus beat linear menus: in Callahan, Hopkins, Weiser and Shneiderman (CHI 1988), users selected about 15% faster with fewer errors, because every item is the same distance away and larger. The cost is screen space.Keep the radial layout, but test a linear control (V6) on Sahi, because our slots are smaller than desktop pie slices.
R2Marking menus (Kurtenbach and Buxton): novices press and wait about ⅓ s for the menu, and experts flick in the remembered direction without waiting. In field use, marks were about 3.5× faster than selecting from the menu. Keeping errors under 10% allows 8 items per level at up to 2 levels.Seven items, one level and a 300 ms hold are in line. Directions must never move between sessions or placements, or experts can’t flick.
R3How people hold phones (Hoober 2013, 1,333 observations): 49% one hand, 36% cradled, 15% two hands.Optimise for one right thumb first, and mirror for left-handed use.
R4Touch accuracy (Hoober 2017): about 7 mm at the centre, 9 mm at the edges and 12 mm in the corners, and people prefer to touch the centre.Anchors and slots near edges and corners (V1, V2, V5) need larger targets than the 6.6 mm a quarter fan gives. Highlighting before release corrects some error, but the study has to measure it.
R5The thumb’s reachable area depends on device size, hand size and grip; the far top corner is the hardest (Bergstrom-Lehtovirta and Oulasvirta, CHI 2014).The index chart’s pill (V1, V6) needs a regrip on 6.1–6.7-inch phones. Anchors at mid-height or lower don’t.
R6Bezel menus started from the screen edge can be fast and eyes-free once learned (Jain and Balakrishnan, CHI 2012). But Android uses both side edges for Back, and lets an app exclude at most 200 dp of each edge and none of the bottom home-gesture area. Apple’s guidelines say not to interfere with system edge gestures.Rule out edge swipes. Any anchor within 24 dp of the right edge, where the slide goes left, will be read as Back on Android. That affects the pill’s right end, the axis corner, the price axis and the dock, which need exclusion rectangles or a hit area moved inwards.
R7Android’s default long-press timeout is 400 ms; AOSP lowered it from 500.A 300 ms hold opens our wheel before any system long-press. The crosshair keeps its own long-press on the candles.
R9Trading apps (Section 16): MetaTrader 5 opens a radial menu for a chart with a single tap (timeframes, indicators, drawings, crosshair, settings). Long-press on a chart is the crosshair in almost every app. In Kite, FYERS, Angel One and IBKR, a hold at a price or on the price axis starts an order at that price.The gesture would be new to traders, so it has to be taught. Keep the candles for the crosshair and keep the wheel off the price axis.
R8Shipped hold-and-slide menus: Procreate’s QuickMenu (six buttons in a radial, touch and drag to select), Pinterest-style hold menus (an arc of actions around the finger, drag and release), iOS pull-down buttons opened by touch and hold (Safari’s Tabs button), Material 3’s FAB menu (2–6 actions that open where the button is), and ThumbMenu (an arc in the bottom-right corner for the thumb).Each placement here borrows a pattern traders have seen in other apps. The FAB guidance also caps a floating menu at six actions; we have seven.

Most of these figures come from the papers’ abstracts and from secondary summaries, not the full texts (the full PDFs weren’t reachable from this environment). Treat the numbers as directional, and check R1, R2 and R6 against the originals before quoting them. Sources are listed in Appendix B.

04 / The screen

The screen the wheel has to live on

The prototype rebuilds the split chart from your screenshots at the size they were taken: an Android phone at 412×915 dp, with Inter for the app chrome and Roboto 12–13 px for the chart labels in TradingView’s default colours (#089981 up, #F23645 down). The visible 5-minute candles of both charts were read off screenshot 4, and the history before them is generated. Screen-by-screen overlays put every text and control within 1–3 px of the original. Appendix A lists the measurements.

05 / Shared rules

Rules every placement shares

Only the anchor, shape and scope change between placements. Everything else is v1.4 behaviour, so the comparison isolates placement.

  • Hold to open. Hold still for 300 ms within 10 px to open the wheel. Moving first hands the touch to the region’s own gesture (scale the axis, resize the split) or cancels (pill, corner, dock). A tap keeps its current meaning: the pill opens the chart menu and the dock opens the Quick actions list.
  • Same seven actions, same order. 1m, 15m, Trend line, Fib retracement, VWAP, EMA 20, Clean view, with the configurable slots from v1.4 at their defaults. Order runs from the slot next to the horizontal outward. In V4 the two halves mirror each other; in V6 the list runs top to bottom.
  • Strict hit test. The inner zone, outside the ring, separators and the current timeframe all cancel. Nothing is clamped, so releasing anywhere that isn’t clearly a slot is a safe cancel.
  • Feedback. A light impact on open, a selection tick when the highlighted slot changes (at most once per 50 ms), a success pattern once the change has applied, and a soft tick on cancel. A readout pill outside the wheel, on the side away from the hand, names the chart and what release will do. The centre of a quarter fan names the chart (Section 15).
  • Labels. Each action has a label, a short label and a full name, fitted by the rules in Section 15. A slot never shows an ellipsis.
  • Fallback. If the wheel doesn’t fit, or its labels don’t fit at the current text size, the hold shows “Not enough room for the wheel” or “Labels don’t fit the wheel at this text size”, followed by “release for Quick actions”. Release opens the list.
  • Interruptions. One wheel at a time. A second finger, losing focus or a sheet opening cancels the gesture.
  • Accessibility. Every action is also in the Quick actions list, opened with a tap from the ⋮ menu, from the dock (V5) or from the fallback.
06 / Placements

The six placements

Each screenshot is the prototype mid-gesture on the reference phone, with the touch point shown. Distances are in millimetres at 1 dp = 0.1588 mm.

V1 · Pill fan Baseline, PRD v1.4

Index chart: holding 5m and sliding to Trend.
AnchorTimeframe pill of each chart (61×24 dp; hit area 69×36).
GestureHold 300 ms. A tap still opens the chart menu.
ShapeQuarter fan down and left. Inner radius 120, outer 264–280 (v1.4 gate).
Acts onThe chart that owns the pill.
FitFits on all four phones with the chart-only layout (R 280). Only just fits in an iPhone Safari tab (R 265–266). Falls back to the list with the order panel open (v1.4 C-01).
ReachIndex 97–129 mm (pill at 14% height): needs a regrip. Option 55–69 mm.
ConflictsNone on its own control. The pill’s right end is within 24 dp of the edge: add a 2 × 24 dp exclusion rectangle on Android.
For
  • Found from a control people already tap
  • Chart choice is explicit
  • Adds nothing to the screen
Against
  • Index chart out of one-handed reach
  • Quarter fan: 6.6 mm targets, 2.54 bits
  • Covers the header and the top of the price axis while open

V2 · Axis-corner fan Per chart, lower

Index chart: holding the corner glyph and sliding to VWAP.
AnchorThe empty cell where the price and time axes meet (about 57×24 dp; hit area 60×38), marked with a small wheel glyph.
GestureHold 300 ms. Moving first cancels.
ShapeQuarter fan up and left (up and right when mirrored for left-handed use). Radius 120–280.
Acts onThe chart that owns the corner.
FitFits on every phone (R 277–280).
ReachIndex 84–100 mm (53% height). Option 36–40 mm.
ConflictsOn the reference Android phone the option chart’s corner sits at 97% height, inside the home-swipe strip, and the slide up-left starts like a home swipe. It must move above the mandatory inset, at least 32 dp from the bottom (for example to the bottom of the price axis). Both corners touch the right-edge back strip: exclusion rectangles of 2 × 38 dp.
For
  • Opens over the chart’s own candles, leaving the header visible so you can watch 5m become 15m
  • Option chart in easy reach
  • Chart choice is explicit
Against
  • A new affordance to learn
  • The corner is the least accurate place to touch (12 mm, R4)
  • Small anchor; the option corner has to move on Android

V3 · Price-axis arc Per chart, at any height

Index chart: holding the price axis and sliding to EMA 20.
AnchorAnywhere on the price axis. The centre of the arc follows the finger’s height.
GestureHold still 300 ms. Dragging scales the axis as it does today.
ShapeHalf ring opening left, radius 56–156, seven slots of 25.7°.
Acts onThe chart that owns the axis.
FitNeeds 164 dp above and below the finger, so it opens on 71–81% of the index axis but only 35–54% of the option axis. Holding near either end falls back to the list.
ReachSet by the user: 39–113 mm.
ConflictsShares the axis with drag-to-scale. On Android the right 24 dp of the axis is the Back strip and the slide goes left, which is a back swipe. The hit area has to stop 24 dp short of the edge, leaving about 33 dp on the index axis and 21 dp on the option axis, and exclusion rectangles can’t cover two full axes (200 dp cap). In Kite, FYERS and Angel One a hold on a price or on the price axis starts an order (Section 16).
For
  • Shortest travel (16.8 mm) and lowest difficulty (1.75 bits)
  • The finger chooses the height
Against
  • Nothing on screen shows it exists
  • Clashes with axis scaling and the Android back swipe
  • Opens on only part of the option axis
  • Other broker apps use a hold on the price axis to place an order (Section 16)

V4 · Split-handle dial Both charts, centre

Holding the split handle and sliding down-left: 15m on the option chart.
AnchorThe handle between the two charts (hit area 60% of the width × 36 dp).
GestureHold 300 ms. Dragging resizes the charts as it does today.
ShapeDial with radius 56–196 (172 on a 360-wide phone). The top half acts on NIFTY50 and the bottom half on the option, with a 12° dead band along the horizontal.
Acts onThe chart in the direction you slide; labels above and below the dial name each half.
FitFits on every phone (R 172–196).
Reach77–94 mm, at the centre of the screen.
ConflictsHold and resize share the handle. Anyone who presses, pauses and then drags to resize will open the dial instead; the study must measure this.
For
  • Both charts from one place, chosen by direction
  • Largest targets (7.1–7.9 mm) and low difficulty (1.83 bits)
  • Centre of the screen is the most accurate place to touch (R4)
  • Adds nothing to the screen
Against
  • The handle reads as “resize”, so the gesture must be taught
  • Only exists in split view (single chart falls back to V1)
  • Sliding across the midline lands in the other chart’s half (mitigated by the dead band)

V5 · Thumb dock One global button

Holding the dock and sliding to VWAP on the option chart, the chart touched last.
AnchorA 44 dp floating button at the bottom right of the option chart, over the price axis.
GestureHold 300 ms. A tap opens the Quick actions list with a chart switch.
ShapeQuarter fan up and left (mirrored for left-handed use). Radius 120–280.
Acts onThe chart touched last. Its card gets an outline and the centre of the wheel names it.
FitFits on every phone.
Reach43–48 mm on every phone, the best of the six.
ConflictsNone with chart gestures. Within 24 dp of the right edge: add a 44 dp exclusion rectangle or move it 12 dp inwards.
For
  • Always in the thumb zone
  • Visible, so it’s easy to discover
  • Works in any layout
Against
  • Chart choice is implicit, so changes can land on the wrong chart
  • A permanent button covers price-axis labels
  • Adds chrome to a crowded screen; Material’s FAB guidance caps a FAB menu at six actions, and we have seven
  • Sits where scalper apps put one-tap Buy and Sell (Section 16)

V6 · Press-drag list Linear control

Option chart: holding 5m and sliding down to VWAP.
AnchorTimeframe pill, as in V1.
GestureHold 300 ms. A list drops below the pill (above it if there’s no room); slide onto a row and release.
ShapeSeven rows of 44 dp (56 at 200% text) in a list 228–340 dp wide, sized to the longest name.
Acts onThe chart that owns the pill.
FitOpens below the pill on the reference phone. On 360×800 and on iPhones the option chart’s list opens above and covers the index chart.
ReachIndex 94–127 mm. Option 60 mm below, 95–111 mm when the list opens above.
ConflictsSame as V1.
For
  • Full names and states, at any length (Section 15)
  • Still works as a gesture at 200% text
  • Scales beyond seven items
  • Looks like Sahi’s own menus
Against
  • Travel grows with each row (row 7 is about 55 mm away)
  • No directional muscle memory
  • R1 predicts it is slower than radial

09 / Recommendation

Recommendation and decision rule

  1. Study shortlist: V1 (control), V4, V5 and V6 (linear control). Add V2 if there’s time, because it’s the fallback if V4’s resize conflict is too high.
  2. Drop V3. It is invisible, it shares its anchor with axis scaling, it collides with the Android back swipe, and it opens on only 35–54% of the option axis.
  3. If shipping before a study: V4 in split view plus V1 everywhere. V4 adds no chrome, makes the chart choice part of the gesture, has the largest targets and fits every phone. V1 keeps the familiar entry and covers single-chart layouts.
  4. Labels and prior art agree. V4 has the most room per slot (61–99 px) and V6 takes full names, so both keep working with long presets. The quarter fans need short labels of about six characters, and at 200% text only V6 still works as a gesture (Section 15). Nothing in trading uses this gesture yet, and a hold on the price axis already means “trade here” in Indian broker apps, which settles V3 (Section 16).
  5. Decision rule: pick the placement with the lowest median time to apply among those that pass every guardrail:
    • Accidental opens: no more than 2% of resize or scale attempts on a shared anchor (V4, V3).
    • Wrong-chart changes: no more than 3% of commits (V4, V5).
    • Wrong actions: no more than 5% of commits.
    • No drop in crosshair, resize or axis-scale use compared with V1.
    • Rated at least as comfortable as V1 for one-handed use.
10 / Validation

Study plan

  • Who: 12–16 Sahi traders who trade F&O on their phones. Half should use the phone one-handed for the session.
  • Design: within-subjects. Each person uses V1, V4, V5 and V6, with order counterbalanced by a Latin square. For each placement: the coach tip, one practice run of the prototype’s Timed tasks, then one measured run (8 tasks in random order).
  • Tasks: switch a chart to 1m or 15m, turn VWAP, EMA 20 or Clean view on, and start a trend line or Fib. Tasks are split across both charts and each starts from 5m with nothing on the chart.
  • Measures (logged by the prototype): time from task shown to commit; wrong actions; cancels; fallbacks; holds that interrupted a resize or scale; one-handed comfort (1–5); and a final ranking. Results are kept on the device and exported as JSON.
  • Devices: participants’ own phones, a mix of Android and iPhone, with the prototype added to the Home Screen so the browser bars don’t take height.
  • Then: run the winner against V1 in a beta build for two weeks, using the analytics in Section 12.
≤ 2%accidental opens on shared anchors
≤ 3%wrong-chart commits
≤ 5%wrong actions
Mediantime to apply decides among passing placements
11 / Requirements

Requirements and acceptance criteria

IDRequirementAcceptance check
PL-01A placement setting selects V1–V6 for testing, behind a feature flag.Switching placement takes effect on the next hold; there’s no restart.
PL-02Every placement opens after 300 ms within 10 px and shows the same seven actions in the same order.Hold, slide and release applies the action on both charts, for all six placements (prototype test: 44 of 44 checks pass).
PL-03Moving before 300 ms gives the touch to the region’s own gesture.V3: dragging the axis scales it. V4: dragging the handle resizes. V1, V2, V5, V6: moving first cancels with no wheel.
PL-04The crosshair keeps the long-press on candles in every placement.Long-press on the candles shows the crosshair and never opens a wheel (checked for all six).
PL-05V4: the top half acts on the index and the bottom half on the option, with a 12° dead band on the horizontal.Releasing on the horizontal cancels with the reason “separator”.
PL-06V5: the dock acts on the chart touched last, which is outlined, and the centre of the wheel names it.Tapping a chart moves the outline; a tap on the dock opens Quick actions for that chart, with a chart switch.
PL-07Android: anchors within 24 dp of a side edge request exclusion rectangles; no anchor’s hold point is inside the bottom mandatory gesture inset.With gesture navigation on, holding and sliding left from V1, V2 or V5 never triggers Back, and V2’s option anchor sits at least 32 dp above the bottom.
PL-08If the wheel doesn’t fit, the hold shows the fallback hint and release opens the Quick actions list.V3 held at the top of the index axis opens the list on release.
PL-09Left-handed setting mirrors V2 and V5.Corner anchor and dock move to the left and their fans open up and right.
PL-10Releasing on the current timeframe changes nothing and says so.The chart stays on its timeframe and the cancel is logged as “current”.
PL-11Analytics carry the placement on every event (Section 12).Every wheel_open, commit and cancel event includes placement and anchor.
PL-12Every action has a label, an authored short label and a full name. For indicators, the short label is the chart legend’s short name.Binding “Bollinger Bands (20, 2)” shows “Bollinger Bands” where it fits and “BB 20 2” where it doesn’t. The readout, V6 and Quick actions show the full name.
PL-13Labels follow the fit order in Section 15 and never show an ellipsis inside a slot.With all four label sets on 412×915 and 360×800, no label, caption or icon crosses its slot and no two labels overlap (prototype: 0 of 63 slots per set).
PL-14Slots of the same kind share a layout: both timeframes keep or drop their caption together, the three on/off actions likewise, and icons appear on every slot or none.No wheel shows icons or state words on some slots of a group and not on others.
PL-15If a slot can’t fit even its short label at 11 px (times the text size), the hold falls back with the reason “labels”.At 200% text every radial placement shows “Labels don’t fit the wheel at this text size”, and release opens Quick actions. V6 still opens its list.
PL-16The readout sits outside the wheel on the side away from the hand, names the chart and the full action, and wraps to two lines at most.The readout never overlaps a slot or the touch point. With “Exponential Moving Average (EMA) 200” it shows two lines.
PL-17V6 sizes its list to the longest full name (228–340 dp) and its rows to the text size. Quick actions rows grow with the text and never clip.“Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP)” fits on one row; at 200% rows are 56 dp, and no Quick actions row clips.
PL-18Settings previews a bound preset’s wheel label and rejects a short label wider than 45 px at 12.5 px Inter Medium (about six characters).Binding “VWAP · weekly” previews the short label “VWAP W” in V1.

13 / Risks

Risks and open questions

IDQuestion or riskHow we resolve it
OQ-1Does the real app use the axis corner, a hold on the price axis, or a hold on the split handle today?Product to confirm. The prototype assumes they are free.
OQ-2Gesture-navigation insets on the phones Sahi traders use.Read the system gesture insets at runtime and lay anchors out from them.
OQ-3Is a permanent floating button acceptable on the chart (V5)?Your call (decision 2 in Section 01).
OQ-4Which placement applies in single-chart view?V1 by default, since V4 needs the split.
OQ-5v1.4’s OD-1: may a wheel extend over the other chart?V4 and V5 do by design; V1–V3 stay within their chart.
RK-1Hold-versus-drag confusion on shared anchors (V3, V4).Measured by the accidental-open guardrail; tune the hold to 350 ms if needed.
RK-2Changes applied to the wrong chart (V5).Outline plus the name in the centre of the wheel; measured by wrong_chart_undo.
RK-3Research figures taken from secondary summaries.Check R1, R2 and R6 against the original papers before external use.
RK-4A hold on the price axis means “place an order at this price” in Kite, FYERS, Angel One and IBKR (Section 16).Drop V3, and keep the wheel off the price axis so Sahi can adopt that convention later.
RK-5V5’s dock sits where scalper apps put one-tap Buy and Sell.With the order panel open, move the dock above it or hide it. Never place it within 16 dp of an order button.
OQ-6Who writes the short labels, and are they translated? Sahi has Hindi tutorials, and FYERS ships seven languages.Content design writes one short label per catalogue item and checks it against the 45 px budget in every language Sahi ships.
OQ-7Should the configurable slots (VWAP, EMA) move to the widest positions?That would give presets about half as much room again in V1, but it breaks “same order in every placement”. Decide after the study.
OQ-8Would traders rather have a favourites row, as in TradingView, MetaTrader 5 and Binance?Ask in the study debrief, and add a favourites-row arm if there is time.
14 / Prototype

Using the prototype

  • Where: prototype/quick-wheel-placements/index.html, a single self-contained file. On a computer, a panel next to the phone switches placement, phone size and options and shows the event log. On a phone, the ⋮ button in the top bar opens the same choices.
  • Links: add ?v=1…?v=6 to open a placement, &frame=small|iphone|max for another phone size, &hand=left for left-handed, &zones=1 for the touch-zone overlay, &touches=1 to show touches, and &coach=0 to hide the first-run tip.
  • What works: all six placements with haptics, the timeframe menu, Settings (all seven chart types and the view toggles), Add indicators (EMA, SMA, VWAP, Bollinger Bands and Key Levels are drawn; search and tabs work), Range, drawing tools, crosshair, pan, pinch, axis scaling, split resizing, the Quick actions list, “Show me how” demos and Timed tasks.
  • What doesn’t: orders, symbol search, Sahi AI, landscape and live prices. The prices on screen are the ones in your screenshots.
  • Haptics: vibration on Android (tap the page once first); a light tick on iOS 18 Safari as a best effort; on-screen pulses and optional sound on a computer.
  • Label stress test: in the ⋮ menu or the panel, choose one of four label sets (Default, Own presets, Any indicator, Full names) and a text size (100%, 130%, 200%). A switch turns the fit rules off to show how v1.0 behaved. Links: &labels=presets|any|full, &text=130|200, &fit=0. A yellow tag at the bottom left shows when a test is on. Only the names change: the chart still draws VWAP and EMA. The panel lists how each slot was fitted.
  • On a real Android phone: V3 and the right ends of V2 and V5 are close enough to the edge that a slide left can trigger Back (R6). That’s the conflict in PL-07, and it shows up in testing too: hold a finger’s width in from the edge.
15 / Stress test

Long names: what happens when a label doesn’t fit

The slots are small, and PRD v1.4 already lets people change what goes in four of them: any interval in the two timeframe slots, and another named preset for VWAP and EMA. If other indicators are allowed later, the names get longer. People who set a larger font on their phone make every name longer. This section stress-tests every place a name appears, in all six placements, and sets the rules the prototype now follows.

What was tested

Label setWhat goes in the slotsExample
DefaultThe shipping labels1m, 15m, Trend, Fib, VWAP, EMA 20, Clean
Own presetsWhat the MVP allows: any interval, another VWAP or EMA preset125m, 1D, VWAP · weekly, EMA 200 · close
Any indicatorIf any tool or indicator can go in a slot (after the MVP)Parallel channel, Fib extension, Supertrend (10, 3), Bollinger Bands (20, 2)
Full namesCatalogue names typed in full, and a long instrumentVolume Weighted Average Price (VWAP), Exponential Moving Average (EMA) 200, NIFTY FIN SERVICE
Text 130% and 200%The default labels at Android font scale 1.3 and 2.0EMA 20 at 16 px and 25 px

Each set ran on all six placements, on both charts, on the 412×915 reference phone and a 360×800 phone. That is 63 slots across nine wheels per set, plus the V6 list, the Quick actions sheet, the chart header and the timeframe pill. A script measures every label, caption and icon against its own slot (text by its ink), checks labels against each other and checks the readout against the centre of the wheel, then takes the screenshots below. Every number in this section comes from that script.

What happened in v1.0

16 of 63slots already spill with the default labels
50 of 63spill with “Any indicator”
93 pxworst spill (full names)
33labels colliding at 200% text
Label setSlots spillingWorstLabels collidingReadout outside the centreV6 rows wrappingQuick actions clipped
Default16 of 637.5 px02 of 800
Own presets26 of 6322.3 px38 of 800
Any indicator50 of 6326 px138 of 82 of 140
Full names49 of 6393.2 px228 of 84 of 140
Text 130%36 of 6315.1 px78 of 800
Text 200%56 of 6332.7 px338 of 88 of 1425.2 px
  • The defaults are already at the limit. “EMA 20” crosses its slot edge by 3.3 px in V1 and 3.6 px in V2 and V5. In V3 the “Timeframe” caption under 1m and 15m spills by up to 7.5 px. v1.4 had flagged EMA 20 (C-02) and asked for “EMA / 20” on two lines; the v1.0 build drew it on one line.
  • Long names run into their neighbours. With “Bollinger Bands” and “Supertrend 10 3”, 50 of 63 slots spill and labels collide 13 times. In the highlighted slot the overflow is black text on the dark neighbour, so the name you’re about to apply is the one you can’t read.
  • The readout in the centre can’t hold a full name, and in V3 and V4 it is under the finger. The centre of those two wheels is the touch point. In the quarter fans the readout has about 90 px; “Turn on Bollinger Bands (20, 2)” needs about 150.
  • V6 holds up best but still breaks. Long names wrap inside 44 dp rows, and a four-character interval (“125m”) overlaps its row title because the icon box is 18 dp wide.
  • At 200% text everything collides (56 of 63 slots spill, 33 collisions), V6 rows overlap, and Quick actions rows clip by 25 px.
  • The chart header and timeframe pill are fine. “NIFTY FIN SERVICE Spot” leaves 107 px before the pill on the reference phone and 55 px on a 360-wide phone; “125m” widens the pill by about 18 px.

The rules the prototype now follows

  1. Every action has three names. The label it asks for in the wheel, an authored short label, and the full name. For indicators the short label is the chart legend’s own short name, the one traders already see on the chart (“BB 20 2”, “ST 10 3”, “EMA 200”). For drawing tools it is a chosen word (“Channel”, “Fib ext”). The full name goes in the readout, the V6 list, Quick actions and the screen-reader label.
  2. Fit in this order; the first that fits wins. The label on one line, then on two lines, broken at a space and never mid-word. Then the short label on one line, then two. Then the same without the state words; the state stays visible as a dot when on, and in words in the readout. Then smaller type, down to 11 px (13 px for intervals) times the text-size setting. Then the same without the icon. Before it shrinks, a label slides along its slot’s centre line to where the slot is wider.
  3. Never an ellipsis in a slot. “VW…” and “EM…” no longer say which action they are. If even the short label doesn’t fit, the wheel doesn’t open. The hold says “Labels don’t fit the wheel at this text size · release for Quick actions”, and release opens Quick actions (v1.4 already sends 200% text there).
  4. One layout per group. Both timeframe slots keep or drop their caption together, and so do the three on/off actions. If any slot loses its icon, every slot does. A wheel where some slots have icons and others don’t looks broken.
  5. The readout moves out of the wheel into a pill on the side away from the hand: above the fan (V1, V2, V5), above the dial (V4) and left of the ring (V3). It names the chart and the full action, wraps to two lines, then ends with an ellipsis, and is at most 340 dp wide. The centre of a quarter fan keeps only the chart name. V3 and V4 show nothing there, because it is under the finger.
  6. V6 grows to fit. The list is 228–340 dp wide, sized to the longest full name. Rows stay on one line with an ellipsis, and their height follows the text size (44 dp, 56 dp at 200%).
  7. Quick actions never clips. Its rows grow with the text, because it is the accessible route.
  8. Chart names in the header end in an ellipsis before they can reach the timeframe pill. The centre, the dial’s labels and the readout use the short chart name (for example FINNIFTY, 23500 CE).

Label budget

The widest one-line label each placement can hold with its icon and state, at 100% text, measured with the fit code. Characters assume an average of 6.7 px per character at 12.5 px Inter Medium; narrow letters fit more.

PlacementNarrowest slotWidest slotTwo linesNote
V1 Pill fan45 px, about 6 (15m, VWAP, EMA)71 px, about 10 (1m)About 6 a line, only in the two slots nearest verticalVWAP and EMA, the slots people can change, are among the narrowest
V2 Axis-corner fan, V5 Thumb dock45 px, about 6 (EMA)70 px, about 10 (Trend)About 5–6 a line, in the three slots nearest vertical
V3 Price-axis arc47 px, about 7 (1m)70 px, about 10 (Trend)About 5–6 a line, end slots onlyThe “Timeframe” captions don’t fit even with the defaults
V4 Split-handle dial61 px, about 9 (Fib)99 px, about 14 (1m, Clean)About 7–8 a line51 px, about 7, on a 360-wide phone
V6 Press-drag list141 px, about 21 (228 dp list)253 px, about 38 (340 dp list)—Full names
Readout pillAbout 40 characters a line, two linesAbout 25 a line in V3, left of the ring

So a short label has to fit 45 px, about six characters, to work in every placement. V4 has about a third more room (61 px), and V6 takes full names.

What this changes

  • Settings must preview the label. When someone binds a preset (v1.4 S2), show how its label sits in the wheel and which short label it will use. Reject a short label wider than 45 px (PL-18).
  • Text size is a placement criterion. At 130% the fans and V3 lose their icons and state words, and V4 keeps its icons. At 200% only V6 still works as a gesture. That favours V4 and V6, the two the recommendation already keeps.
  • In V1 the slots people can change sit in the tightest positions (VWAP at 122°, EMA at 109°). The timeframe slots, whose labels are never longer than four characters, have the widest. Swapping them would give presets more room in V1, but would break the same order in every placement (OQ-7).
  • The readout is now where people read the action. Its position is part of each placement’s spec, and it must never cover the slot being highlighted.
16 / Prior art

Does anyone do this in trading apps?

No trading app we found uses a hold, slide and release menu (a marking menu) for chart tools. The closest is MetaTrader 5’s radial chart menu, which opens with a tap. Around it, two conventions are close to universal: a long-press on the chart shows the crosshair, and in Indian broker apps a long-press on a price, or on the price axis, starts an order at that price. Otherwise, apps give quick access to intervals and tools with favourites bars.

AppGestureWhat it doesWhat it means for Sahi
MetaTrader 5 (MetaQuotes), Android, iPhone and iPadTap on the chartOpens a radial menu for that chart: switch timeframe, add indicators, add objects (drawings), crosshair, chart settings. A long-press on a position or order line opens its context menu. A long-press in the timeframe menu adds a period to the quick-access bar.The closest precedent, with almost the same actions, so radial chart menus are familiar to forex and CFD traders. It opens with a tap and you tap an item, so experts can’t flick, and it never competes with a long-press.
TradingView appLong-press; tap a starLong-press shows the crosshair, and a “+” at the price adds an alert or an order (third-party guides). In one-tap trading mode a long-press on the chart sets an order’s price. Favourite intervals, indicators and drawing tools sit in a quick-access bar.Crosshair on long-press is the norm, and Sahi already follows it. Favourites bars are the main alternative to a wheel.
Zerodha Kite (TradingView charts in the app)Long-pressLong-press enables the crosshair. Trade from Charts: long-press a price level, then choose a limit or stop-loss order.To Kite users, holding at a price means “trade here”.
FYERSLong-press a price levelA “+” appears on the price axis; tap it, choose the order type, quantity and price, and confirm. A swipe right on a watchlist symbol shows a chart shortcut.The same convention, on the price axis itself.
Angel OnePress and hold the price on the right-hand axisOpens the order pad with that price filled in, on by default (the web app uses a “+”).Exactly where V3 would sit.
Kotak NeoTap the “+” at a priceTrade from Charts order form.The same convention, tap-based.
Interactive Brokers (IBKR Mobile)Tap and holdCrosshair, then a “+” next to the price creates an order at that price.The same convention outside India.
cTrader MobileLong-press; single tapLong-press shows the crosshair, then a measure mode. A single tap opens chart tools. A draggable floating panel holds orders, positions and chart objects. Drawing tools moved to bottom sheets and gained text labels “for easier identification”.A floating panel on the chart (like V5) has shipped. Labels were added to tool icons, which supports keeping labels in the wheel.
NinjaTrader mobileHold at a price in the SuperDOM, then confirmPlaces a stop order at that price. On the desktop, right-clicking the chart offers Buy and Sell Limit and Stop.Holding at a price means orders here too.
RobinhoodLong-press; swipe upLong-press scrubs the chart and sets a limit or stop price; orders are submitted with a swipe up. In 2016 it used 3D Touch to preview a stock and add it to a watchlist.VoiceOver users found swipe-to-submit hard, which is why every wheel action also has a tap route (Quick actions).
moomooLong-pressLong-press a drawing tool to add it to Favourites; long-press a drawing’s point to get a magnifier.Favourites again. Long-press configures; it doesn’t run actions.
BinanceLong-pressLong-press the coin list for a quick action menu, and the bottom navigation to customise the home screen. On the web, favourite intervals sit in the top bar.Hold for actions is familiar on lists, not on charts.
DhanType on the chartTyping a number sets an x-minute timeframe; custom timeframes can be marked as favourites.A keyboard shortcut, not a touch gesture.
Groww 915 and Scalper, Punch, Sahi Options ScalperOne tapOrder panels under or beside split charts: one-tap buy and sell, stop-loss and target on the chart. Punch calls its panel a “Scalper Joystick”, but it is a one-tap panel, not a gesture.The bottom of a scalper screen is where order buttons live, which is where V5’s dock sits.
Quick Suite TradingLong tap on a quoteA “Quick Action Menu”: add to a watchlist, open an order ticket.A hold-to-open quick action menu, but on quotes.
TakeProfit (mobile web)Drawing on a phoneA virtual touchpad over the chart, so the finger doesn’t hide the point being placed.Finger occlusion is a known problem on phone charts. The readout pill moves away from the finger for the same reason.

What it means for the wheel

  • It would be new to traders. No app we found uses hold, slide and release on a chart, so the gesture has to be taught (coach tip, “Show me how”). MetaTrader 5 shows that traders accept a radial chart menu with these same actions.
  • Keep the candles for the crosshair. Every app we looked at uses a long-press on the chart for the crosshair or for scrubbing. That matches Sahi and rules out a hold on the candles, as Section 08 already does.
  • The price axis is the market’s “trade at this price” gesture. Kite, FYERS, Angel One, IBKR and TradingView all start an order from a hold at a price. A chart-tools wheel on the axis (V3) would surprise traders coming from those apps, and would stop Sahi from adopting the same order gesture later. That is one more reason to drop V3 (RK-4).
  • Keep the dock away from order buttons. Indian scalper screens put one-tap Buy and Sell at the bottom. V5’s dock must never sit over or next to them; when the order panel is open it moves up or hides (RK-5).
  • Favourites bars are the real competitor. TradingView, MetaTrader 5, Binance, Dhan and moomoo let traders pin favourite intervals or tools one tap away. The study should ask whether traders would rather have a favourites row than any wheel (OQ-8).
  • Labels matter. cTrader added text to its drawing-tool icons to make them easier to identify, which supports keeping labels in the wheel, not only icons, as Section 15’s rules do.

The descriptions come from the companies’ help pages, release notes and app-store notes, plus a few third-party guides, found by web search; the pages themselves couldn’t be opened from this environment. Gestures change between app versions, so check them in the current apps before quoting. Sources are in Appendix B.
